standard_prerequisites.name: The pointwise free version of the flat along the fibre lemma
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-finite-type-flat-at-point-free, invoked at proof line 3585
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces, for each point of the fibre, an elementary etale neighbourhood and an affine etale neighbourhood of the point whose global sections of the pulled back module are free over the base, with the residue fields preserved; the passage from finitely many such pieces to one global neighbourhood is what the counted proof supplies.

standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of an elementary etale neighbourhood dominating finitely many given ones
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Morphisms, label more-morphisms-lemma-elementary-etale-neighbourhoods, invoked at proof line 3607
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies one elementary etale neighbourhood of the base dominating the finitely many neighbourhoods attached to the chosen points, which is what makes the disjoint union of the pieces into a single neighbourhood.

core_obligations: Apply the pointwise lemma at the points of the fibre: for each point x of the fibre X_s find an elementary etale neighbourhood of the base and an etale neighbourhood Y_x of x over the base change, affine of finite presentation over the localisation of the base, with the pulled back module of finite presentation and with free global sections, and note in particular that the image of the fibre of Y_x is an open neighbourhood of x in the fibre (proof lines 3583-3600).

Pass to finitely many points: since the fibre is quasi-compact, choose finitely many points whose neighbourhoods cover it, and then choose one elementary etale neighbourhood of the base dominating all of them (proof lines 3601-3607).

Assemble the global neighbourhood: define X' as the disjoint union of the pieces Y_{x_i} base changed to the dominating neighbourhood, with the obvious morphism to X; by construction the fibre is covered by its image and the global sections of the pulled back module are the direct sum of the base changes of the pointwise free modules, hence free over the new base; the remaining verifications are said by the author to be minor details (proof lines 3608-3623).
proof_roadmap: Cover the fibre by the pieces supplied by the pointwise lemma (proof lines 3583-3600).
Choose a single dominating elementary etale neighbourhood (proof lines 3601-3607).
Take the disjoint union of the base changed pieces and compute its global sections (proof lines 3608-3623).
difficulty_reason: The lemma globalises the pointwise flat along the fibre statement: for a finite presentation morphism and a finite type module flat at every point of a fibre, there is an elementary etale neighbourhood of the point of the base and an affine etale neighbourhood of the fibre, on which the pulled back module is finitely presented and has free global sections (statement lines 3556-3581, tag 05L0). The proof applies the pointwise lemma at each point of the quasi-compact fibre, passes to finitely many points, chooses one elementary etale neighbourhood dominating all the pointwise ones, and then takes the disjoint union of the base changed pieces, checking that the global sections are a direct sum of base changes of free modules. The assembling step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
